title: Activation and SJLJ runtime
summary: An MVS single-task setjmp/longjmp frame seam substitutes for C++ exception transfer in the cfront bootstrap. Dev20 fail-closes invalid and duplicate frame lifecycle operations; native API catch wrappers release frames only once. Host selection, negative-path and cfront micro-probe checks are distinct from target ABI testing.
invariants: setjmp must execute within the matching live catching function, never within a helper frame that has returned.
An unmatched exception must terminate; silent normal return is invalid.
A 32-bit pointer container is not proof that the MVS target can address beyond 24 bits.
Single-task bootstrap state is not a reentrant, multithreaded or target MVS ABI qualification.
Future task-local frame binding and true MVS jump-buffer layout require independent guest proof.
